case.pattern_description: Coordinated multi-card abuse conducted through a specific mobile device profile (Samsung SM-G935F on Chrome 62) operating behind an anonymous proxy. The device connects to multiple unrelated customer cards in rapid succession, generating one or two mid-value online purchases per card with 'New' device status. This behavior bypasses conventional real-time model scoring but matches an established device ring with 100% historical fraud confirmation.

evidence.claim: Rule R9: Undocumented patterns: Rule R9: Undocumented patterns. When activity fits none of the known patterns but the evidence shows coordinated or repeated abuse across customers, recommend `CREATE_CASE`, `FILE_REPORT`, and `ESCALATE_TO_ANALYST`, and describe the pattern in your own words. Do not force it into a known category.

Rule R6: Shared origin: Rule R6: Shared origin. When several cards show fraud from the same device profile, the same billing region, or the same recipient email in one window, name the shared element, recommend `CREATE_CASE` and `FILE_REPORT`, and `MONITOR_CONNECTED_CARDS` for every card that shares it.

case.summary: Online transaction 3467764 ($156.58) on card C10193-K2 was flagged for utilizing device D004630, which is associated with fraud ring 57672119. Device D004630 is linked to four prior confirmed-fraud closed cases (CC-2649, CC-2985, CC-2971, CC-3035) and has appeared as a new device behind an anonymous proxy across nine cards in 30 days. Although the transaction produced a low model score of 0.036 and cardholder non-authorization has not yet been reported, the cross-card device pattern indicates coordinated multi-account abuse. The finding is assessed as uncertain with a 0.192 probability, escalating to an analyst for cardholder verification while monitoring eight connected cards.
